_about: Rivals: the other families on the island, and the men who carry their messages.

scenes.title: One of {rboss.last}'s men drinks on your side
scenes.text: {man.call} has been drinking at the Hialeah on Pacific three nights running, on your side of the avenue, alone. He works for {rboss.call}. Your bartender says he tips like a man who wants to be noticed, and complains about his boss like a man who wants to be overheard.

choices.label: Buy him a drink and listen

hook.why: Talked out of turn about his boss

choices.result: By the third drink {man.first} had told you which of {rboss.first}'s numbers banks is behind on its ice.
choices.failText: {man.first} drank your liquor and told {rboss.first} about it in the morning.

choices.label: Have him walked to the corner

opinion.why: Threw my man out of a bar

scenes.title: At Bracelin's funeral home
scenes.text: Old man Fiorello's wake, and every family on the island signs the book. {rboss.call} arrives late with four men and stops at your pew. Loud enough for the widow: "Your {capo.first} still collecting for you? Somebody has to."

choices.label: Say nothing. Not at a wake.
choices.hint: The old women will remember who kept his dignity.

opinion.why: Let him say that about me

choices.label: Answer him, quietly, so only he hears
choices.result: {rboss.first} went pale and signed the book with a shaking hand.
choices.failText: {rboss.first} laughed, a wake-house laugh, and the whole room heard it.

scenes.title: A cannoli from {rboss.first}
scenes.text: A white box from Pagano's bakery, tied with string, left on the hood of your car outside St. Ann's. Inside, a dozen cannoli and a card in {rboss.call}'s own hand: "Life is short. The season is shorter. Coffee?"

choices.label: Coffee, then
choices.result: Two hours over coffee. Nothing written down. Everything understood.
choices.failText: Two hours over coffee, and you both left knowing exactly where the other one stands: apart.

choices.label: Eat the cannoli. Send a thank-you note and nothing else.
